description: New service-to-service auth boundary ships with only happy-path unit tests. High risk; escalate to risk-based coverage. Grounds: 'depth scales with impact', 'API tests are first-class'.
input: PR introduces a token-exchange endpoint between two services; tests cover only a valid token. No expired/invalid/replay cases, no consumer-driven contract test.

expected.recommend: add negative-path API tests (expired/invalid/replay) and a Pact contract test before merge

description: Destructive DB migration lacks a rollback/idempotency test. High-risk NFR gap.
input: PR adds a migration that drops and recreates an index on a large table, with no test exercising rollback or re-run idempotency and no performance note.

expected.recommend: add rollback + idempotency tests and capture a migration-duration NFR estimate

description: Pure refactor with strong existing coverage and no behavior change. the QA Lead must NOT manufacture risk. Grounds: 'risk vs value'.
input: PR renames internal variables and extracts a helper in a module already covered by comprehensive unit tests; diff is behavior-preserving.

expected.recommend: no additional tests required; existing coverage is sufficient

description: E2E depends on a live third-party endpoint, causing nondeterminism. Flakiness/isolation issue.
input: PR's new E2E hits a real external payments sandbox over the network in CI; it fails ~10% of runs when the sandbox is slow.

expected.recommend: stub/mock the external dependency at the boundary (or contract-test it) so CI is deterministic

description: Payment capture path tested only for success; missing failure/idempotency/edge. High risk on money path.
input: PR adds card-capture handling; tests cover a successful capture only — no declined-card, no duplicate-submit/idempotency-key, no partial-refund path.

expected.recommend: add declined, duplicate-submit (idempotency), and refund cases before merge — money paths are high-impact

description: Tests execute code but assert nothing meaningful, inflating coverage. Reward-hack-resistant: high coverage != quality.
input: PR raises line coverage to 95% by adding tests that call functions and assert only that no exception is thrown (no output/behavior assertions).

expected.recommend: coverage is gamed; require behavioral assertions on outputs/side-effects, not exception-free execution
